newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries end unchanged to higher.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries end unchanged to higher.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries closed unchanged to slightly higher on Tuesday as investors took a mildly defensive stance before the release on Wednesday of September consumer price data.

The 6-3/4 percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond, which advanced in the first part of the session, gradually retreated, briefly sinking into negative territory before edging back into the plus column.
The bellwether 30-year bond ended at 98-26/32, up 1/32, to yield 6.84 percent, versus 6.85 percent at Friday's close.
U.S. government securities markets were closed on Monday to market the Columbus Day holiday.

"It was a very, very quiet session overall," said William Sullivan, senior vice president and economist at Dean Witter Reynolds. "The market tried to register improvement early in the day but there was no followthrough of consequence."
Sullivan said the cause of the market's mild malaise was "a little bit of nervousness about tomorrow's CPI."
The government will release the October Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters foresee a 0.3 percent rise in the index.

The economists estimated, on average, that the September core CPI, the index without its more volatile food and energy items, would also be up 0.3 percent. Both the overall and core CPI edged up only 0.1 percent in August.
Sullivan noted that the U.S. Labor Department had commented earlier this month about potential upward biases in some areas of the September CPI.
"A bit of defensiveness came into the market, but nothing substantive," he said. "Key support held in all areas."
"People were waiting for the CPI on Wednesday," said Joshua Feinman, vice president and economist at Bankers Trust.
